what_happened: The the person running Athena ran two jobs by hand: d103 (resume from a kept candidate) and hydf (a re-read of m30w). Drains 30 to 35 kept stopping with nothing landed, because of lost reader errors and disk stops. m30w is the job that fixes lost reader errors, and it could not get through a drain. No job was rejected and no criterion or check was evaluated in this event.
cause: Athena has no recovery path that is separate from the normal drain. The drain stops on a reader error that is not recorded, and on disk stops, and it has no quarantine, bounded retry or skip for one item. Nothing ranks a job that repairs the drain ahead of the jobs that trigger the fault, or runs it with isolation. It is the same defect that blocks it. Nothing detects that several drains in a row landed nothing, so the loop continues until the the person running Athena notices. Resuming from a kept candidate and re-reading a job are manual steps with no supported automatic form.
prevention: Three changes together. (1) Drain records the reason for every reader failure (error, timeout, empty output) in the job record and drain output. It skips or quarantines an item after a bounded number of retries, so one bad item cannot stop the queue. (2) Drain treats a disk stop as a pause that cleans up and resumes, not as a stop. (3) Drain counts consecutive drains that landed nothing and, past a threshold, runs a designated repair job first, resuming from a kept candidate or re-reading automatically, and tells the the person running Athena why it did so.
proposed_request: Make queue drain survive reader failures and disk stops, so a stuck item cannot block the fix for itself. Outcomes: (1) When the reader returns no reading, the reason (error, timeout, empty output or refusal) is written to the job record and shown in the drain output. (2) After a set number of failed reads, drain sets the item aside as quarantined, carries on with the other items, and lists the quarantined item at the end. (3) A disk stop pauses the job, frees space that Athena can safely reclaim, and resumes it without marking the job failed. (4) After N consecutive drains that land nothing, drain runs a job that is marked as a drain repair first, resumes it from its kept candidate if one exists, and prints why it reordered. Acceptance: tests with a fake reader that fails with each reason show the reason recorded and the other items landing, a test with a simulated low-disk stop shows pause and resume, and a test replays the case of a repair job that sits behind a failing item and shows the repair job landing first. Do not change the planner's dependency rules.
